P.h: Attackers hijack three country TLDs to mint fake Google certificates
P.p: Attackers took control of the .gh, .sl and .as country code domains and altered authoritative DNS records. That let them pass the automated domain control validation that certificate authorities run, and obtain unauthorized TLS certificates for several Google domains and other major brands.
P.s: Google blocked the known certificates in Chrome. Domain owners should monitor certificate transparency logs and publish restrictive CAA records.

items.h: Citrix NetScaler SAML zero-day is under active exploitation
items.d: CVE-2026-88779 crashes ADC and Gateway appliances with one crafted request. CISA confirmed exploitation. Apply the fixed build, start with SAML-enabled Gateway and AAA servers, and treat a clean IOC script result as inconclusive.
The postinstall script stole AWS, GitHub, Kubernetes and Vault credentials and opened a reverse shell. Downgrade to 5.8.2, rotate every credential, kill manifest-cache.js.

items.h: Atlassian Data Center flaw rated 9.3, no login needed
items.d: CVE-2026-21589 exposes files in the web root of Bitbucket, Confluence and other products. Patch immediately or restrict external access.

items.h: GitHub Copilot CLI runs malware from a poisoned README
items.d: The env command is on the read-only allowlist, so curl piped to sh never triggers approval. GitHub called it a known issue and declined a bounty.

P.h: Meta and Sierra publish an open protocol for personal AI agents
P.p: The Personal Agent Protocol defines how consumer AI agents deal with businesses: authentication, consumer control, and visibility for companies over what agents do across websites, APIs and company agents. Genesys, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart are named partners.
P.s: Microsoft also made Execution Containers generally available, letting developers fence what files, networks and resources an agent can touch. It launched alongside the Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra.

tiles.t: MCP agent-to-agent flaws end in SSRF
tiles.d: Google and four others fixed bugs where an injection on one agent was forwarded to others over MCP. Severity ran from 2.7 to 8.

tiles.t: Anthropic opens a three-tier Cyber Verification Program
tiles.d: Defense, Red Team and Specialized access tiers, replacing Project Glasswing.
Unauthorized edits and millions of requests, no compromise found.

tiles.t: AWS AgentCore default bash tool runs as root
tiles.d: Unit 42 scanned the heap and exfiltrated the AgentCore Identity JWT. The same harness hands agents their identities.

tiles.t: Fake AI ad portals steal MFA codes
tiles.d: Phishing sites posed as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude ad tools.

P.h: Cloudflare ships 46 launches in Birthday Week 2026
P.p: Highlights include a new command-line interface called cf, an open-source pipeline named Forge, and a plan to become a public certificate authority while preparing its cryptography for the post-quantum era. A beta Monetization Gateway lets creators charge AI agents for content using HTTP 402.
P.s: For pipeline owners, Google's guide to hardening CI/CD recommends ephemeral runners, short-lived OIDC credentials, immutable dependency references and provenance checks.

tiles.t: GitHub rebuilds Git for agent-scale writes
tiles.d: Decoupled storage on Azure Blob and less push coordination give up to 35x write throughput.

tiles.t: kubectl cp can write to a Windows Startup folder
Node swap is GA in Kubernetes
tiles.d: Up to 3x density in tests with local SSD swap.

tiles.t: Kubernetes 1.35 refuses to start kubelet on cgroup v1
tiles.d: Check kernel and runtime support, align cgroup drivers, and update monitoring that reads cgroup files directly.

items.h: DNS root key rolls over October 11
items.d: Only the second root KSK rollover ever. Operators of DNSSEC-validating resolvers should confirm they trust KSK-2024 or risk resolution failures.

items.h: Claude Haiku 5.5 arrives at $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens
items.d: Price rises 5x past 100,000 tokens, where GPT-6 Luna looks cheaper. Below that it matches Luna's price with higher benchmarks.

items.h: OpenAI posts 372 math results, few humans can read them
items.d: Experts say the proofs are so poorly written they need AI help to follow, and the citations are often irrelevant.

items.h: Apple readies LG-built doorbell, lock and thermostat
items.d: Launching October 13 under the LG brand, with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread and Matter, around Apple's new smart home hub.
